Option B’s balanced points system risks diluting these protections by mixing economic and humanitarian criteria, potentially sidelining urgent rights claims. Option B’s balanced points system (H 35, S 35, F 20, C 10) aligns well with this by incorporating high-skill matches (S) and family reunification (F), which have positive fiscal impacts, alongside humanitarian needs (H). Option A risks inefficiency by allocating ≥50% to H + C, where C has a negative fiscal impact (-$10k). Option C’s focus on U cases with negative impact (-$20k) and delayed allocation may reduce immediate welfare gains. Thus, B offers a better cost-benefit balance and aggregate welfare.
